name: ISAI
summary: A tabletop search for axions from solar iron-57 nuclear transitions, independently testing axion–nucleon coupling.
detection_principle: Solar 14.4 keV axions are resonantly absorbed by an enriched iron-57 target; an XRPIX silicon-pixel detector reads out de-excitation X-rays.

status.label: Prototype experiments / R&D
status.evidence: 2023 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: ISAI, Investigating Solar Axion by Iron-57: the experiment

collaboration.name: ISAI Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: A 2023 report describes commissioning and initial observations; projected sensitivity is not evidence for axion discovery.

science_scope: Primarily searches for solar-produced axions or hidden photons as complementary tests of dark-matter candidates. Solar flux is distinct from cold Galactic-halo dark matter; a solar-axion discovery alone would not establish the composition of cosmic dark matter.
